rationale: Tests conceptual understanding of the neurotic-psychotic dichotomy after the content section that introduces it — specifically the distinction based on reality testing, anchored away from the micro_quiz at block 5 which covers preserved-insight OCD.

Tests recall of a specific ICD-11 structural fact — the chapter housing mental disorders — immediately after the ICD-11 overview content block (index 7). Distinct from existing micro_quizzes which test organic vs functional reasoning and specific diagnoses.

Apply-level question on the bedside utility of psychiatric classification, anchored after the Clinical Significance block (index 10). Presents a scenario requiring the student to use the organic-functional and neurotic-psychotic axes together to determine the clinically correct first step — not covered by any existing micro_quiz.

Analyze-level question on psychiatric history-taking structure, anchored after the content block detailing history domains (index 5). Requires the student to identify which domain of the psychiatric history is being neglected in a clinical vignette — distinct from micro_quiz at block 6 which tests MHCA 2017 confidentiality.

Apply-level question on interpreting MSE findings for a differential diagnosis, anchored after the Interpreting MSE Findings block (index 9). The scenario differs from block 10's delirium micro_quiz: this one contrasts mania vs psychosis using affect and thought-form findings from the MSE.

Evaluate-level question on a specific, commonly misunderstood provision of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 — the right of a person with mental illness to make an advance directive. Anchored after the Applied Practice block (index 11). This is factually distinct from block 6's micro_quiz on confidentiality (which addresses family involvement, not advance directives).
